messages.content: How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?

function.name: calculate_projectile_range
function.description: Calculate the range of a projectile launched at an angle with initial velocity, using the kinematic equation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity at which projectile is launched. This is a float type value.

angle.description: The angle at which projectile is launched. This should be in degrees. This is a float type value.

time.description: The time in seconds after which the range is to be calculated. This is a float type value.

message.content:
**Horizontal distance travelled in a given time**

If a car (or any projectile) is launched from the ground with an initial speed \(v\) at an angle \(\theta\) above the horizontal, the horizontal component of its velocity is

\[
v_x = v \cos\theta .
\]

Assuming no horizontal forces (e.g., no air resistance or friction), this component stays constant. Therefore, after a time \(t\) the horizontal distance \(x(t)\) from the launch point is simply

\[
\boxed{\,x(t)=v\,\cos\theta \; t\, } .
\]

---

**Vertical motion (for reference)**

The vertical component of the velocity is \(v_y = v \sin\theta\). With gravity \(g\approx9.81\;\text{m/s}^2\) acting downward, the vertical position is

\[
y(t)=v\,\sin\theta \; t-\frac12 g t^2 .
\]

---

**If you want the total distance along the trajectory**

The instantaneous speed is

\[
v_{\text{inst}}(t)=\sqrt{(v\cos\theta)^2+\bigl(v\sin\theta-g t\bigr)^2},
\]

so the arc‑length from launch to time \(t\) would be

\[
s(t)=\int_0^t v_{\text{inst}}(t')\,dt'.
\]

This integral has no simple closed form, but for short times it is close to \(v t\) (the straight‑line distance).

---

**Quick sanity check**

- If \(\theta=0^\circ\) (horizontal launch), \(x(t)=v t\) as expected.
- If \(\theta=90^\circ\) (vertical launch), \(\cos\theta=0\) so \(x(t)=0\); the car moves only vertically.

So, for a horizontal distance travelled in a given time \(t\), use \(x(t)=v\cos\theta\,t\).
